sources.title: RFC 5545 — Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.locator: §3.2.19 TZID; §3.3.5 DATE-TIME; §3.8.2.4 DTSTART; §3.8.3.1 TZID; §3.8.4.4 RECURRENCE-ID; §3.8.4.7 UID; §3.8.5.1 EXDATE; §3.8.5.3 RRULE; §3.8.7.4 SEQUENCE
sources.observed_operation: Read the normative recurrence, identifier, time-zone, exception and revision sections; no implementation was executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A local DATE-TIME without TZID is floating; fixed local times use UTC or local time with time-zone reference. Each TZID used requires a matching VTIMEZONE with valid coverage for every recurrence. RECURRENCE-ID names the original occurrence start. EXDATE excludes values from the recurrence set. UID is persistent and globally unique. SEQUENCE is initialized at 0 and monotonically increments on significant revisions when used.
sources.applicability: Normative iCalendar semantics for the proposed feed and optional .ics snapshot; does not establish that any named commercial client implements every recurrence feature identically.

critic_review.access_utc: UNKNOWN per individual request; source access fell within the review window recorded below
critic_review.observation: Directly reopened RFC 5545. Checked floating versus TZID time, VTIMEZONE coverage, UID, original-start RECURRENCE-ID, EXDATE, weekly RRULE examples, and SEQUENCE.

reviser_review.observed_operation: Reopened the exact IETF Datatracker RFC page through the web tool and read the abstract and relevant sections. Response receipt was timestamped immediately after retrieval; no server or client was operated.
reviser_review.governing_condition_default_exception: A calendar collection may be created through provisioning (including account provisioning) or by MKCALENDAR. CalDAV servers must support WebDAV ACL access control. The RFC does not require that every participant be provisioned with an orchestra-member account.
reviser_review.applicability: Supports a standards-level server-sync comparison and the qualified account wording. It does not determine the authentication/account model of an unselected CalDAV service or validate a deployment.

sources.locator: Abstract; §3 synchronization-token overview; `sync-collection` operation and example reports
sources.observed_operation: Read protocol definition and token-based routine synchronization example.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Client presents a previous sync token; server returns changed, added or deleted collection resources and a new token. First synchronization requests a full listing. It requires compatible WebDAV server and client support.
sources.applicability: Explains the distinction between change-aware server synchronization and periodic `.ics` feed polling.

reviser_review.locator: §3.2 DAV:sync-collection report implementation and advertisement; §§3.4–3.5 initial and subsequent synchronization; §4 sync-token property
reviser_review.observed_operation: Reopened the exact IETF Datatracker RFC page through the web tool and read the sync-collection implementation condition and token/change behavior. Response receipt was timestamped immediately after retrieval; no implementation was executed.
reviser_review.governing_condition_default_exception: The server must advertise the DAV:sync-collection report only if that report is implemented for a collection. Where supported, the server tracks additions, changes and removals and issues opaque state tokens; an expired token may require full synchronization.
reviser_review.applicability: Supports a conditional analogous synchronization mechanism, not an assertion that every WebDAV or CalDAV deployment implements it or that it guarantees push/immediate refresh.
